text:
jamie: FYI support ticket from Acme. They rotated a dashboard API key and now get 401 invalid_api_key when calling /v1/generate. UI still shows the old key as "active".
jamie: customer-provided curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-redwood","prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response: 401 {"error":{"message":"Invalid API Key","type":"invalid_api_key"}}

elena: do we have a request-id from their attempt? also need org id and the key id that shows in their dashboard (they pasted a partial key id like key_abc123)

jamie: they sent request-id: req_01H0A9Z8 and org: org-acme-42. key id in UI: key_abc123. Pasting backend auth log we pulled for req_01H0A9Z8:
```
[2024-11-12T09:16:07Z] req=req_01H0A9Z8 auth: key_id=key_abc123 result=denied reason=revoked revoked_at=2024-11-12T09:15:23Z revocation_reason=auto_revoke_inactive
```

ops-bot: audit-log: actor=system policy=auto_revoke_inactive target=key_abc123 timestamp=2024-11-12T09:15:23Z metadata={inactivity_days:90}

devon: looks like the key was auto-revoked by our org policy (90d inactivity). The dashboard cache was serving stale state for ~5-10m which made it still appear in the UI as "active" after revocation. We're aware this is confusing.

ejamie: (typo) jamie: thanks. Can we restore or un-revoke the key for the customer? They rotated but wanted a rollback.

elena: we don't support un-revoking keys as a security rule. Can issue a new key for them or have admin create a new one. Short-term mitigation: tell customer to create a new dashboard key and update their clients. If they need an immediate rollback, we can create a replacement key that matches previous name but new id.

devon: ops note: we should add stronger UI hints — show last-revoked timestamp and policy that triggered the revocation. Also add a small TTL on cached key status (reduce to 30s) to avoid the "visible-but-revoked" window.

jamie: I relayed to customer: create a new key and deploy. I also offered to issue a temp key from support if they can't rotate fast enough. Customer asked for repro steps so they can audit: we've included backend log lines and audit id 0x7c9f for their ticket.

jamie: closing loop here — repro summary to attach to ticket:
- Action: dashboard auto-revoke applied by policy (auto_revoke_inactive) at 2024-11-12T09:15:23Z
- Symptom: API calls return 401 invalid_api_key with backend log showing key_status=revoked
- UI: key remained visible due to cache for ~5-10m after revoke
- Fix: create new key and update clients; cannot unrevoke existing key; engineering will shorten cache TTL and surface revocation reason in UI

devon: thx, marking for product follow-up (tracker: PROD-7321) and ops follow-up to create temporary support key process if needed. :thumbsup:
